newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Brash says NZ economy rebounded in June quarter.
newsitem.headline: Brash says NZ economy rebounded in June quarter.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Don Brash told a Parliamentary Committee on Wednesday that the economy may have rebounded somewhat in the June quarter after initial estimates in GDP data this week showed it had contracted by 0.5 percent in the March quarter.

Giving a debriefing on Friday's RB June Monetary Policy Statement to the Finance and Expenditure Committee, Brash said that although the bank had forecast 0.3 percent growth in the March quarter in the statement it already realised the economy may have contracted somewhat in the March quarter, Brash said.
Statistics New Zealand said on Monday the economy contracted 0.5 percent in the March quarter.

"Indicators for the June quarter however, together with out own business contacts, suggested that the economy may have rebounded somewhat in the quarter just ended and we projected that growth would strengthen in subsequent quarters," he told the committee.

Asked to comment on the difference between the RBNZ's 0.3 percent GDP forecast for March and the much lower out-turn, Brash told parliament, "It is a very large amount -- I share the discomfiture of my colleagues.
"The general market perception was a 0.1 percent increase. I don't think anyone was expecting a figure as low as negative 0.5 percent," he added.

Brash said he thought there were three factors in play that led to the lower-than-expected number for the March quarter -- a switch from hydro power to thermal generation as lake levels fell, the timing of Easter, which meant that roughly five
percent fewer working days in the March quarter usual, and the fact there was a much higher stock kill (by livestock farmers) in the December quarter, meaning there was less supply in March.
